chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Fudayl from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him, 'What is the condition (option of inspection) in animals?' He said, 'Three days for the buyer.' I asked, 'What is the condition in non-animals?' He said, 'The two sellers have the option as long as they have not separated; and when they separate, there is no option after their mutual satisfaction.'

key_terms.اَلشَّرْط: Condition (specifically the option of inspection or 'khiyar al-shart')
key_terms.اَلْبَيِّعَانِ: The two sellers/parties to the sale
key_terms.اِفْتَرَقَا: They separated (from the meeting place of the transaction)
key_terms.بِالْخِيَار: With the option (right to cancel or confirm)

ai.seo_question: What is the duration of the inspection period for buying animals versus other goods in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the foundational principles of 'khiyar al-shart' (option of condition) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between the fixed three-day inspection period for livestock and the immediate binding nature of contracts for other goods once parties separate. It highlights the scholarly emphasis on transparency and the right to rescind a deal before finalization, a concept deeply rooted in the Prophet’s practice as recorded in major Sunni and Shia sources. The ruling underscores the importance of mutual consent and the prevention of hidden defects in commercial transactions.
